Rashi on Pesachim 62b:10:1.hebrew: בהדי דקא שקיל ואזיל א"ל - ר' שמלאי לר' יוחנן:
Rashi on Pesachim 62b:10:1.english: As he was taking leave to go, he said to him - Rabbi Simlai to Rabbi Yochanan.

Rashi on Pesachim 62b:10:2.hebrew: מה בין לשמו ושלא לשמו לאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו - מאי שנא דלשמו ושלא לשמו פסול, לאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו כשר:
Rashi on Pesachim 62b:10:2.english: What is [the difference] between for its own sake and not for its own sake, [and] for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it - Why is it different that [when slaughtered] for its own sake and not for its own sake it is disqualified, [whereas when slaughtered] for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it it is valid?

Rashi on Pesachim 62b:11:1.hebrew: פסולו בגופו - מחשבה בגופו של קרבן, אבל מחשבת אוכליו פסול דבר אחר הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 62b:11:1.english: Its disqualification is in itself - [It is] an intention concerning the body of the offering, whereas an intention concerning those who eat it is a disqualification of another matter.

Rashi on Pesachim 62b:12:1.hebrew: אי אפשר לברר - דמה חלק לשמו ומה חלק שלא לשמו? אבל אוכליו אפשר לברר: חלק אוכליו לצד זה, וחלק חולה וזקן בצד אחר. אי נמי, לברר אם אמת מחשבתו, אם אין בה ממש — כגון יאכילנו לראויין, ונמצאת מחשבתו בטילה למפרע, ולשאינן ראויין יחזור דמיהן. וכך שמעתי:
Rashi on Pesachim 62b:12:1.english: It is impossible to distinguish - For which part is for its own sake and which part is not for its own sake? However, [for] those who can eat it, it is possible to distinguish [the parts]: the portion of those who can eat it to this side, and the portion of a sick or elderly person to the other side. Alternatively, [it means] to clarify whether his intention is genuine [or] whether there is no substance to it — for example, he feeds it to those who are fit [to eat it], and his intention is retroactively found to be void, and for those who are not fit, their money is returned. And so I have heard.

Rashi on Pesachim 62b:13:1.hebrew: אינו בארבע עבודות - דאין מחשבת אוכלין בזריקה. מחשבת אכילה לא שייכא בקרבן ציבור, דלא שייכא אלא בפסח:
Rashi on Pesachim 62b:13:1.english: [It] does not [apply] in four services - For there is no intent regarding eaters during the sprinkling [of the blood]. Intent regarding eating is not applicable to a communal offering, as it is only applicable to the Paschal offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 62b:15:1.english: Their strength was weakened - For the reasons of the Torah that were in it were hidden from them.

Rashi on Pesachim 62b:16:1.hebrew: מאצל לאצל - שני מקראות הן, ופרשה גדולה ביניהן. "ולאצל ששה בנים", וקא חשיב ואזיל הבנים, וסיפא דפרשתא "אלה בני אצל":
Rashi on Pesachim 62b:16:1.english: From Azel to Azel - They are two verses with a large section between them: [both begin,] "And Azel had six sons," and [Scripture] goes on to enumerate the sons, and the end of the passage is "these are the sons of Azel."

Rashi on Pesachim 62b:1:1.hebrew: היכא אישתראי - טומאת בשר לאכילה? אפילו קרבן ציבור שדוחה טומאה, הני מילי להקרבה, אבל למיכלה בטומאה לא; דתנן בכיצד צולין (דף עו:): חמשה דברים באין בטומאה ואין נאכלין בטומאה כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 62b:1:1.english: Where was it permitted - [i.e.,] impurity of the meat for eating? Even [in the case of] a communal offering, which overrides impurity, that applies only to offering [it], but to eat it in [a state of] impurity — no; as we learned in a Mishnah in [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin (76b): Five things are brought in [a state of] impurity, and are not eaten in [a state of] impurity, etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 62b:3:1.hebrew: שמתחלתו לא בא - לא נאמרה הבאת עיקר פסח אלא לאכילה. וכי שרייה רחמנא לאיתויי בטומאה ברוב ציבור — כדכתיב "איש איש כי יהיה טמא וגו'", איש נדחה לפסח שני ואין ציבור נידחין — אדעתיה למיכליה שרייה:
Rashi on Pesachim 62b:3:1.english: For from its outset it did not come - The bringing of the Paschal offering itself was stated only for eating. And when the Merciful One permitted bringing it in [a state of] impurity when a majority of the community [is impure] — as it is written, "Any man who shall be impure, etc.": an individual is deferred to the second Pesach, whereas a community is not deferred — He permitted it with the intention of eating it.

Rashi on Pesachim 62b:4:1.hebrew: שעברה שנתו - שנולד אשתקד קודם ראש חודש ניסן והפרישו לשם פסח, וכי מטא ראש חדש ניסן ועברה שנתו, תו לא חזי לפסח, דכתיב זכר בן שנה, וקאי לשלמים, כדילפינן בפירקין דלקמן (פסחים ד' ע:): פסח בשאר ימות השנה שלמים הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 62b:4:1.english: That has passed its year - That it was born last year before Rosh Chodesh Nisan and he set it aside for the sake of a Pesach [offering]; and when Rosh Chodesh Nisan arrived and its year passed, it is no longer fit for a Pesach [offering], as it is written, "a male in its first year," and it stands as a peace-offering, as we derive in our chapter later on (Pesachim 70b): a Pesach [offering] during the rest of the days of the year is a peace-offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 62b:4:2.hebrew: ושחטו בזמנו לשמו - גרס, דהוה ליה שוחט שלמים לשם פסח בזמנו:
Rashi on Pesachim 62b:4:2.english: And he slaughtered it at its [appointed] time for its [own] sake - [This is] the reading, for it is [a case of] one who slaughters a peace-offering for the sake of a Paschal offering at its [appointed] time.

Rashi on Pesachim 62b:4:3.hebrew: ר' אליעזר פוסל - טעמא מפרש בפ"ק דזבחים: ומה פסח שמותרו בא שלמים, שחטו לשם שלמים בזמנו — פסול, שלמים שאין מותרן בא פסח, שחטן לשם פסח בזמן פסח — אינו דין שפוסל:
Rashi on Pesachim 62b:4:3.english: Rabbi Eliezer disqualifies - The reason is explained in the first chapter of Zevachim: Just as a Paschal offering — whose remainder is brought as a peace-offering — if one slaughters it for the sake of a peace-offering in its [proper] time, it is disqualified; [so too] peace-offerings — whose remainder is not brought as a Paschal offering — if one slaughters them for the sake of a Paschal offering at the time of the Paschal offering, is it not logical that it is disqualified?

Rashi on Pesachim 62b:4:4.hebrew: ורבי יהושע מכשיר - דכל זבחים שנזבחים שלא לשמן כשירין, חוץ מפסח וחטאת. ואי משום דנשחטו לשם פסח, קל וחומר הוא: ומה שלא בזמנו, שאינו כשר לשמו, אחרים כשירים לשמו; בזמנו, שהוא כשר לשמו, אינו דין שיכשרו אחרים לשמו? וכל טעמייהו התם מפרש:
Rashi on Pesachim 62b:4:4.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua validates [it] - For all sacrifices that are slaughtered not for their own sake are valid, except for the Paschal offering and a sin-offering. And if [you ask] because they were slaughtered for the sake of a Paschal offering, it is an a fortiori inference: If [when a Paschal offering is] not at its [appointed] time, when it is not valid for its own sake, other [offerings] are valid [when slaughtered] for its sake; [then] at its [appointed] time, when it is valid for its own sake, is it not logical that other [offerings] should be valid [when slaughtered] for its sake? And all their reasons are explained there.

Rashi on Pesachim 62b:5:1.hebrew: שלא בזמנו - לא פסיל ליה ר' אליעזר אם שחטו לשם פסח, כדאמר ליה ר' יהושע: "ומה שלא בזמנו שאינו כשר לשמו, אחרים כשירים לשמו", ולא מיהדר רבי אליעזר: "לדידי, שלא בזמנו נמי אחרים פסולים לשמו". ואמאי? לרב חסדא דאמר לחומרא אמרינן "הואיל", נימא הכא: הואיל ואלו זמנו הוה ושחיט לשמו מיפסיל, הכא הכי נמי ליפסיל, כדקאמר גבי ערל: הואיל ואי הוה מל פסיל, השתא נמי פסיל:
Rashi on Pesachim 62b:5:1.english: Not at its [proper] time - Rabbi Eliezer does not disqualify it if one slaughtered it for the sake of a Pesach offering, as Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: "If not at its [proper] time, when it is not valid [when slaughtered] for its own sake, other [offerings] are valid [when slaughtered] for its sake," and Rabbi Eliezer did not reply: "According to me, not at its [proper] time as well, other [offerings] are disqualified [when slaughtered] for its sake." But why? According to Rav Chisda, who says that we apply [the principle of] "since" (ho'il) for stringency, let us say here: since if it were its [proper] time and one slaughtered [it] for its sake it would be disqualified, here too it should likewise be disqualified — just as he said regarding an uncircumcised person: since if he were circumcised it would disqualify, now too it disqualifies.

Rashi on Pesachim 62b:7:1.hebrew: שלא בזמנו שהוא כשר לשם אחרים - דנפקא לן לקמן (פסחים דף ע:) מוזבחת פסח צאן ובקר, דפסח שניתותר לאחר הפסח קרב שלמים. ואף קודם הפסח נמי נפקא לן בפ"ק דזבחים מקרא אחרינא, מואם מן הצאן קרבנו לזבח שלמים, דבר הבא מן הצאן — דהיינו פסח — יהא לזבח שלמים:
Rashi on Pesachim 62b:7:1.english: Not at its [proper] time, when it is valid for the purpose of other [sacrifices] - For we derive later (Pesachim 70b) from "And you shall slaughter the Pesach [offering] ... flock and herd," that a Pesach [offering] that was left over after Passover is offered as a peace offering. And even before Passover, we also derive [this] in the first chapter of Zevachim from another verse, from "And if his offering from the flock is for a sacrifice of peace offerings": something that comes from the flock — that is, a Pesach [offering] — shall be for a sacrifice of peace offerings.

Rashi on Pesachim 62b:7:2.english: Other [sacrifices] are valid for its sake - For its disqualification [when offered] for the sake of others and the disqualification of others [when offered] for its sake are juxtaposed [in Scripture].

Rashi on Pesachim 62b:8:1.english: Book of Genealogies - A baraita on [the Book of] Chronicles.

Rashi on Pesachim 62b:8:2.hebrew: אין שונין ספר יוחסין לא ללודים כו' - לדחוייה איכוון. ל"א, לפי שאינן מיוחסין:
Rashi on Pesachim 62b:8:2.english: We do not teach the Book of Genealogies neither to Lodites, etc. - He intended to put him off. Another explanation: Because they are not of pure lineage.

Rashi on Pesachim 62b:9:1.english: He took a clod - Mote [in Old French] (a clod of earth).

Rashi on Pesachim 62b:9:2.english: She did not fulfill her obligation - She was unable to learn it in three years.

Tosafot on Pesachim 62b:10:1.hebrew: מה בין לשמו ושלא לשמו לאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו - תימה: מאי קא בעי? הא גמר לעיל מקרא דמקצת אוכלים לא פסלי. ונראה לרשב"א דמיבעיא ליה: אמאי לא גמרינן לשמו ושלא לשמו דכשר מלאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 62b:10:1.english: "What is [the difference] between for its own purpose and not for its own purpose, [and] for those who can eat it and those who cannot eat it?" - [This is] astonishing: what is he asking? Behold, it was derived above from a verse that partial eaters do not disqualify [the offering]. And it appears to the Rashba that he is asking: why do we not derive [that an offering slaughtered] for its own purpose and not for its own purpose is valid from [the case of] for those who can eat it and those who cannot eat it?

Tosafot on Pesachim 62b:13:1.hebrew: לשמו ושלא לשמו ישנו בציבור כו' - תימה לר"י: מאי איריא דאינו בציבור? תיפוק ליה דאפי' ביחיד אינו נוהג אלא בפסח גרידא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 62b:13:1.english: "[The intent that it be] for its own purpose and for a different purpose applies to communal [sacrifices]," etc. - This is astonishing to R"I: Why does [the Gemara] specifically state that [the disqualification of "for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it"] does not apply to communal [sacrifices]? Let it be derived [already] that even for an individual [sacrifice], it applies only to the Paschal offering alone.

Tosafot on Pesachim 62b:14:1.hebrew: פסולו בגופו ואי אפשר לברר איסורו חדא מילתא היא - דס"ל דאי לאו טעמא דאי אפשר לברר איסורו, לא קרי ליה בגופו הואיל ומחשבה היא כדלעיל; אבל ר' יוחנן לא דייק בהכי, וקרי ליה שפיר פסולו בגופו. ושינוי בעלים נמי אי אפשר לברר איסורו, ולהכי לא קחשיב ליה לעיל:
Tosafot on Pesachim 62b:14:1.english: "Its disqualification is in itself and it is impossible to identify its prohibition are one thing" - For [Rav Ashi] holds that were it not for the reason that it is impossible to identify its prohibition, one would not call it [a disqualification] "in itself," since it is [only] an intent, as [noted] above; however, Rabbi Yochanan is not exacting about this, and readily calls it "its disqualification is in itself." And [with] a change of owners as well, it is impossible to identify its prohibition, and therefore he did not count it above.

Tosafot on Pesachim 62b:17:1.hebrew: ערלים למולים נמי ליתיה לכולה ערלה - משמע דהוה ניחא ליה אי הוה תני בתרוייהו כשר. וא"ת: אדרבה, בתרוייהו הוה ליה למיפסל, דהא ר"מ אית ליה מפגלים בחצי מתיר, ואחרים היינו רבי מאיר! וי"ל: דלא אמר פיגול בחצי מתיר אלא במפרש סימן ראשון או שני לערלים, דהוי דבר מסויים, כדמוכח בפ"ב דזבחים (ד' ל.) — ובקונטרס הביאה — אמר ליה אביי: מי סברת אינה כו', ישנה לשחיטה מתחלה ועד סוף, דאמר סימן ראשון חוץ לזמנו וסימן שני חוץ למקומו; ולמה ליה לפרושי? הוה ליה למימר בסתם! אלא ודאי לא אמר ר' מאיר מפגלי' בחצי מתיר אלא במפרש. ועוד נראה, דאפילו אמר בחצי סימן — לאו כלום היא, אלא דווקא בסימן שלם; דפריך התם: והרי קמיצה דכי לחצות דמי, ופליגי! ומשני: התם נמי דאמרי' קומץ דמנחה חוץ לזמנו, דלבונה חוץ למקומה. והרי קומץ דמנחת חוטא דליכא לבונה, ופליגי! ומשני: לא פליגי כו'. ואמאי לא קאמר דפליגי דאמר חצי קומץ חוץ לזמנו וחצי חוץ למקומו? אלא על כרחיך דבר המסוים ושלם בעינן:
Tosafot on Pesachim 62b:17:1.english: [When he has in mind] the uncircumcised before the circumcised, there is also not "all uncircumcised" - This implies that [the Gemara] would be satisfied if [the baraita] had taught that it is valid in both cases. And if you ask: On the contrary, it should have disqualified it in both cases, for Rabbi Meir holds that one can render an offering piggul with half of a matir [permitting factor], and Aḥerim is Rabbi Meir! One can answer: He only said [that there is] piggul with half of a matir when one specifies the first or second siman [i.e., trachea or esophagus] for the uncircumcised, which is a distinct, identifiable entity, as is proven in the second chapter of Zevachim (30a) — and in the Kuntres [i.e., Rashi], [Rashi] brought [that passage]: Abaye said to him, "Do you think [that slaughter] is not... etc. [Rather,] slaughter takes effect from the beginning to the end," where he said [during] the first siman "beyond its time," and [during] the second siman "outside its place." Now why did [the Gemara there] need to specify [each siman]? It should have stated it without specification! Rather, it is certain that Rabbi Meir only said that one can render an offering piggul with half of a matir when one specifies [a distinct entity]. Furthermore, it appears that even if he stated [his intention] regarding half of a siman, it is nothing at all; rather, [it applies] specifically to a complete siman. For [the Gemara] asks there: "But what about kemitzah [taking a handful of the meal-offering], which is like halving [the matir], and yet they disagree?" And it answers: "There too, it is where we say [he had in mind] the handful of the meal-offering beyond its time, [and] that of the frankincense outside its place." "But what about the handful of a sinner's meal-offering, where there is no frankincense, and yet they disagree?" And it answers: "They do not disagree, etc." Now why does [the Gemara] not say that they disagree where he said "half the handful beyond its time and half outside its place"? Rather, perforce we require something distinct and complete.

Tosafot on Pesachim 62b:4:1.hebrew: ורבי יהושע מכשיר - ואע"ג דאיכא מאן דאמר פסח בשאר ימות השנה בעי עקירה, בעברה שנתו מודו כ"ע דהיינו עקירתו, ושלמים לשם פסח שחיט:
Tosafot on Pesachim 62b:4:1.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua validates [it] - Even though there is one who says [that] a Paschal offering during the rest of the days of the year requires uprooting [of its original designation], when its [first] year has passed, everyone agrees that this [itself] is its uprooting, and [thus] he is slaughtering a peace-offering for the sake of a Paschal offering.

Tosafot on Pesachim 62b:5:1.hebrew: לימא הואיל ובזמנו פסול כו' - פי': שיכול להמתין עד זמנו ויפסל. ולמאי דמסקינן בריש שני שעירים (יומא סב:) דאין מחוסר זמן לבו ביום לגבי הואיל, נרא' לפר' דמבו ביום פריך, דשלא בזמנו משמע אפי' בי"ד שחרית, ולהכי פריך: הואיל בזמנו בו ביום פסול, שלא בזמנו נמי פסול:
Tosafot on Pesachim 62b:5:1.english: "Let us say: Since at its [proper] time it is disqualified, etc." - Explanation: because he can wait until its [proper] time and it will be disqualified. And according to what we conclude at the beginning of [the chapter] Shnei Se'irim (Yoma 62b), that there is no [status of] "lacking time" on the same day with respect to [the principle of] ho'il ("since"), it appears [proper] to explain that [the Gemara] is asking from [the case of] "on the same day," for "not at its [proper] time" implies even on the morning of the fourteenth [of Nisan]; and therefore [the Gemara] asks: Since at its [proper] time on that day it is disqualified, [when slaughtered] not at its [proper] time it is also disqualified:

Tosafot on Pesachim 62b:6:1.hebrew: שאני התם דאמר קרא הוא - וא"ת: והא מק"ו דריש ליה רבי אליעזר בפ"ק דזבחים (ד' יא.): "ומה פסח שמותרו בא שלמים כו'", כדמייתי בקונטרס? וי"ל: דע"י ק"ו משמע ליה לר' אליעזר דהוא בהוייתו יהא — לא הוא לשם אחרים ולא אחרים לשמו; ועל ידי כך דריש דשלא בזמנו, דכשר לשם אחרים, אחרים כשרים לשמו, דהא איתקוש אהדדי. אבל אי לאו ק"ו, לא הוה דרשינן אלא לא הוא לשם אחרים ותו לא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 62b:6:1.english: It is different there, as the verse says: "It" - And if you ask: But Rabbi Eliezer derives it from a kal vachomer [a fortiori inference] in the first chapter of Zevachim (11a): "Now if the Paschal lamb, whose remainder is brought as a peace-offering, etc.," as [Rashi] cites in the Kuntres? And one can answer: That through the kal vachomer, it is implied to Rabbi Eliezer that "it" shall be as it is — neither it for the sake of other [offerings], nor other [offerings] for its sake; and through this he derives that [a Paschal lamb slaughtered] not in its [proper] time, which is valid [when slaughtered] for the sake of other [offerings], other [offerings are likewise] valid [when slaughtered] for its sake, for they are compared to one another. However, were it not for the kal vachomer, we would only derive "not it for the sake of other [offerings]," and nothing more.
